title: The finite fibre component has a clopen image in the integral closure
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite-type map of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and write $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$ (a finitely generated $A/I$-module); let $\varepsilon=(1,0)\in B/IB$, so $C_1=\varepsilon(B/IB)$ and $C_2=(1-\varepsilon)(B/IB)$. Let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ (the elements of $B$ that are roots of monic polynomials with coefficients in the image of $A$), let $\phi:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q\cap B'$, be induced by this inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ be the set of inverse images of the primes of $C_1$ under the surjection $B\to B/IB\to C_1$; similarly $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is the set $V(IB')$ of primes containing $IB'$. Suppose $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is open, $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$, and the induced morphism $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (a homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms on all section rings and local rings). Then $\phi(T)$ is open and closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')$, its inverse image under $\phi$ is exactly $T$, and the resulting product decomposition $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$ has $C'_1\to C_1$ an isomorphism and maps $C'_1$ into $C_1$ and $C'_2$ into $C_2$. Precisely: there is a unique idempotent $\varepsilon'\in B'/IB'$ such that $\phi(T)$ is the set of primes of $B'$ containing $IB'$ and not containing a (any) lift of $\varepsilon'$; with $C'_1=\varepsilon'(B'/IB')$ and $C'_2=(1-\varepsilon')(B'/IB')$, the ring map $B'/IB'\to B/IB$ induced by the inclusion sends $\varepsilon'$ to $\varepsilon$, and its restriction $C'_1\to C_1$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex:2529-2541, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH: image of T is open in the closed fibre, finite-over-the-base gives closedness, then clopen-to-product decomposition and factor identification. The exact cited Algebra tags are 00HZ (going-up-closed), 00GU (integral going-up), and 00EE (disjoint clopen product).

proof.text: Notation. Let $\iota:B'\to B$ be the inclusion, so $\phi=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$, $\phi(\mathfrak q)=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Put $R=B/IB$, $R'=B'/IB'$, with quotient maps $\pi:B\to R$, $\pi':B'\to R'$; since $\iota(IB')\subseteq IB$, $\iota$ induces $\bar\iota:R'\to R$ with $\bar\iota\pi'=\pi\iota$. The image of $A$ in $B$ lies in $B'$ (an element $\bar a$ is a root of $X-\bar a$), so $A\to B$ factors as $A\to B'\xrightarrow{\iota}B$ and $IB$ is generated by $\iota$ of the image of $I$ in $B'$. Choose $\tilde e\in B$ with $\pi(\tilde e)=\varepsilon$. The surjection $\beta:B\to C_1$, $b\mapsto\varepsilon\pi(b)$, has kernel $L=\pi^{-1}((1-\varepsilon)R)=IB+(1-\tilde e)B$ (the kernel of $r\mapsto\varepsilon r$ on $R$ is $(1-\varepsilon)R$, since $r=\varepsilon r+(1-\varepsilon)r$). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], $T=\operatorname{Spec}\beta(\operatorname{Spec}C_1)=V(L)$, a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Moreover $T=V(IB)\cap D(\tilde e)$: a prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$ contains $\tilde e(1-\tilde e)\in IB$ (as $\varepsilon^2=\varepsilon$), hence contains exactly one of $\tilde e,1-\tilde e$ (not both, their sum being $1$), so $\mathfrak q\supseteq L$ iff $\tilde e\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), more-algebra.tex:2529-2541; T is the closed subset Spec(C_1) of Spec(B), 'Since T is open in psi^{-1}(V(I))'

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$: $\phi(\mathfrak q)\supseteq IB'$ if and only if $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$. Indeed if $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$ then $\iota(IB')\subseteq IB\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $IB'\subseteq\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; conversely if $IB'\subseteq\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ then $\mathfrak q$ contains $\iota$ of the image of $I$ in $B'$, which generates $IB$ (step 1). Thus $\phi^{-1}(V(IB'))=V(IB)$, and in particular $\phi(T)\subseteq V(IB')$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), more-algebra.tex:2529-2541; the diagram psi = psi' o phi, (psi')^{-1}(V(I)) = Spec(B'/IB')

proof.text: $\phi(T)$ is open in $V(IB')$ (subspace topology). Let $W=\phi^{-1}(U)\cap D(\tilde e)$; it is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ because $\phi=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$ is continuous [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $W\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$. Since $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a homeomorphism (hypothesis), $\phi(W)$ is open in $U$, hence in $\operatorname{Spec}B'$. We claim $\phi(T)=\phi(W)\cap V(IB')$. If $\mathfrak q\in T$ then $\mathfrak q\in\phi^{-1}(U)$ (hypothesis) and $\tilde e\notin\mathfrak q$ (step 1), so $\mathfrak q\in W$, and $\phi(\mathfrak q)\in V(IB')$ (step 2). Conversely if $\mathfrak q\in W$ and $\phi(\mathfrak q)\supseteq IB'$, then $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$ (step 2) and $\tilde e\notin\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\in V(IB)\cap D(\tilde e)=T$ (step 1). Hence $\phi(T)$ is the intersection of $V(IB')$ with an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), more-algebra.tex:2529-2541; 'we conclude that phi(T) is open in U cap (psi')^{-1}(V(I)). Thus phi(T) is open in (psi')^{-1}(V(I))'

proof.text: $\phi(T)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B'$. Let $\rho=\beta\iota:B'\to C_1$. Since $C_1$ is a finitely generated $A/I$-module, every $c\in C_1$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A/I$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], i.e. in the image of $A$ under $A\to B\to C_1$; as $A\to B$ factors through $\iota$ (step 1), this image lies in $\rho(B')$. So $\rho$ is integral, and $\operatorname{Spec}\rho:\operatorname{Spec}C_1\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is a closed map [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map]; in particular its image, the image of the closed subset $\operatorname{Spec}C_1$, is closed. By functoriality $\operatorname{Spec}\rho=\phi\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ ($\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\iota^{-1}(\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak Q))$), and the image of $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ is $T$ (step 1), so this image is $\phi(T)$. Being closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ and contained in $V(IB')$ (step 2), $\phi(T)$ is closed in $V(IB')$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), more-algebra.tex:2529-2541; 'since C_1 is finite over A/I it is finite over B'. Hence phi(T) is a closed subset of Spec(B') by Algebra, Lemmas 00HZ (going-up-closed) and 00GU (integral-going-up)'

proof.text: The decomposition. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] applied to $\pi'$ (kernel $IB'$), $\operatorname{Spec}\pi'$ is a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ onto $V(IB')$. By steps 2--4, $\phi(T)\subseteq V(IB')$ is open and closed in $V(IB')$, so $S'=(\operatorname{Spec}\pi')^{-1}(\phi(T))$ is open and closed in $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\pi'(S')=\phi(T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] there is a unique idempotent $\varepsilon'\in R'$ with $D(\varepsilon')=S'$; for any lift $g_0\in B'$ of $\varepsilon'$ this says $\phi(T)=V(IB')\cap D(g_0)$ (a prime $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ of $R'$ omits $\varepsilon'$ iff $\pi'^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak p})$ omits $g_0$), which is the uniqueness claim of the statement. Put $C'_1=\varepsilon'R'$, $C'_2=(1-\varepsilon')R'$; these are rings with identities $\varepsilon'$, $1-\varepsilon'$, and $r\mapsto(\varepsilon'r,(1-\varepsilon')r)$ is a ring isomorphism $R'\cong C'_1\times C'_2$ with inverse $(x,y)\mapsto x+y$ (this is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00EM, lemma-disjoint-implies-product). The surjection $B'\to C'_1$, $b\mapsto\varepsilon'\pi'(b)$, has kernel $K'=\pi'^{-1}((1-\varepsilon')R')=IB'+(1-g_0)B'$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] and the argument of step 1, $\operatorname{Spec}(C'_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is $V(K')=V(IB')\cap D(g_0)=\phi(T)$.

By Algebra, Lemma 00EM we get a corresponding product decomposition B'/IB' = C'_1 x C'_2'; the idempotent form is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00EE, algebra.tex lemma-disjoint-decomposition

proof.text: $\phi^{-1}(\phi(T))=T$. Clearly $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(\phi(T))$. Conversely, let $\phi(\mathfrak q)=\phi(\mathfrak t)$ with $\mathfrak t\in T$. Then $\phi(\mathfrak q)\in\phi(T)\subseteq U$, so $\mathfrak q\in\phi^{-1}(U)$, and $\mathfrak t\in\phi^{-1}(U)$ by hypothesis; $\phi$ is injective on $\phi^{-1}(U)$ (a homeomorphism onto $U$), so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak t\in T$.

proof.text: Choice of $g$ (as in the source, and as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-fibre-choose-g], steps 2--3, whose statement cannot be cited here because it assumes the conclusion $C'_1\cong C_1$). With $g_0$, $K'$ as in step 5, $V(K')=\phi(T)\subseteq U$ (hypothesis $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$). Write $\operatorname{Spec}B'\setminus U=V(J)$ for an ideal $J$ (definition of the Zariski topology). Then $V(J+K')=V(J)\cap V(K')=\emptyset$, i.e. the $D(r)$, $r\in J+K'$, cover $\operatorname{Spec}B'$, so $J+K'=B'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i); write $1=j+k$, $j\in J$, $k\in K'$. Put $g=g_0j$. Since $\varepsilon'^2=\varepsilon'$, $g_0(1-g_0)\in IB'$, so $g-g_0=-g_0k\in g_0IB'+g_0(1-g_0)B'\subseteq IB'$: thus $\pi'(g)=\varepsilon'$ and $K'=IB'+(1-g)B'$. As $g\in J$, $D(g)\cap V(J)=\emptyset$, i.e. $D(g)\subseteq U$.

proof.text: $B'_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism (as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-fibre-choose-g], steps 4--5). $\phi=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$ has $\iota$ as its map on global sections under $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B',\mathcal O)=B'$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so by the second clause of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] $\phi^{-1}(D(g))$ is the principal open $D(\iota(g))=D(g)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0) the restriction maps $B'\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B'}(D(g))$ and $B\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}(D(g))$ are localizations at $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; identify these section rings with $B'_g$ and $B_g$. Since $D(g)\subseteq U$ (step 8) and $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], $\phi^\sharp_{D(g)}:B'_g\to B_g$ is a ring isomorphism; it commutes with restriction from global sections, where it is $\iota$, so it is the unique ring map with $b/1\mapsto\iota(b)/1$, namely $\psi:b/g^n\mapsto\iota(b)/g^n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), more-algebra.tex:2529-2541; 'Then B'_g -> B_g defines a homeomorphism on spectra and an isomorphism on local rings (by our choice of U above). Hence it is an isomorphism'

proof.text: $C'_1\to C_1$ is an isomorphism. Let $K=IB+(1-g)B$. As $\pi(\iota(g))=\bar\iota(\pi'(g))=\bar\iota(\varepsilon')=\varepsilon$ (step 7), $g$ is a lift of $\varepsilon$, so $K$ is the kernel of $\beta:B\to C_1$ (step 1, with $\tilde e=g$), and $K'$ is the kernel of $B'\to C'_1$, $b\mapsto\varepsilon'\pi'(b)$ (steps 5, 8). Since $\bar\iota(\varepsilon'\pi'(b))=\varepsilon\pi(\iota(b))$ (step 7), under $C'_1\cong B'/K'$ and $C_1\cong B/K$ the restriction $C'_1\to C_1$ of $\bar\iota$ is the map $\bar\iota_1:B'/K'\to B/K$ induced by $\iota$. Now $1-g\in K'$, so the image of $g$ in $B'/K'$ is $1$, a unit; by the universal property of $B'_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] the quotient map factors through $\lambda':B'_g\to B'/K'$, $b/g^n\mapsto\bar b$, which is surjective with kernel $K'B'_g$ (if $\bar b=0$ then $b\in K'$ and $b/g^n=(b/1)(1/g^n)\in K'B'_g$; conversely $\lambda'$ kills the generators $k/1$, $k\in K'$). Likewise $\lambda:B_g\to B/K$, with kernel $KB_g$. The isomorphism $\psi$ of step 9 sends $k/1$ to $\iota(k)/1$, and $K$ is generated by $\iota(K')$ (it is generated by $\iota$ of the image of $I$ in $B'$, step 1, and $1-g=\iota(1-g)$), so $\psi(K'B'_g)=KB_g$ and $\psi$ induces an isomorphism $B'_g/K'B'_g\cong B_g/KB_g$ with $\lambda\psi=\bar\iota_1\lambda'$. Hence $\bar\iota_1$, and so $C'_1\to C_1$, is an isomorphism.
